subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support a Slack act-as-user mode that receives user-level events and replies through an xoxp token without the Slack APP badge?
rationale: The request is technically plausible but changes who OpenClaw is allowed to impersonate in Slack and how powerful user tokens are selected for inbound and outbound work.

options.title: Require explicit act-as-user opt-in
options.body: Add a clear account-level mode with scope checks, authorization mapping, docs, and live Slack proof before enabling user-token inbound/reply behavior.

options.title: Use existing userTokenReadOnly semantics
options.body: Treat `userTokenReadOnly: false` as sufficient for act-as-user replies, accepting that existing configs may gain broader identity behavior than they currently imply.

options.title: Decline regular-user impersonation
options.body: Keep Slack replies on the bot/App identity and document the bot-DM workaround as the supported security boundary.

recommendation.title: Require explicit act-as-user opt-in
recommendation.body: Add a clear account-level mode with scope checks, authorization mapping, docs, and live Slack proof before enabling user-token inbound/reply behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across Slack account/auth/routing surfaces and CODEOWNERS context for sensitive repository decisions.
